title: Evaluation of a Systematic Set of Interdental Brushes Based on Passage Hole Diameter (PHD) Size Distribution - an in-vivo Pilot Study
summary:
The aim of this study is to evaluate a new systematic set of interdental brushes in terms of reliability of size selection and satisfaction among patients and therapists. What is new about this set of brushes is that the size distribution is based on the so-called passage hole diameter instead of the ISO sizes used previously. The passage hole diameter is defined as the smallest hole diameter through which a brush can be guided with clinically relevant force. All interdental brushes available on the market can be classified according to the passage hole diameter. Laboratory studies have shown that interdental brushes based on this system ensure effectiveness and comfort and cover a wide range of sizes. This study aims to transfer these findings into clinical practice.
Either geriatric patients, patients with periodontitis, or patients with at least three active carious lesions requiring treatment will be invited to participate in the study. This classification will be used to evaluate the use of interdental brushes in several patient groups.
Three appointments are planned for the study, each 3-6 months apart. At the first appointment, a routine dental examination will be carried out and oral hygiene will be checked. In addition, 12 examiners will fit interdental brushes, take a digital impression of the oral cavity using a scanner, and have participants fill out three questionnaires on oral health literacy, oral health-related quality of life, and their experience with the comfort and user-friendliness of the interdental brushes.  After receiving instructions on how to use the interdental brushes, patients will receive a supply of the selected interdental brushes for use at home. 
At the second and third appointments, the examination and oral hygiene check described above will be repeated, and the questionnaires on oral health literacy and oral health-related quality of life will be filled out again. Another questionnaire asks questions about the extent and regularity of use as well as satisfaction with the use of interdental brushes during the observation period. At the third appointment, a new digital impression is taken. Digital impressions are taken at the beginning and end of the study period to document tooth movement, tooth substance loss, or possible gum recession. In addition, routine clinical data collected as part of their standard treatment (e.g., age, body weight, general medical conditions) will be used for this study.

interventions.name: Evaluation of the handling and satisfaction with the PHD-based set, evaluation of the parameters for gingival/periodontal health over a period of 6–12 months, and evaluation of the reliability of size selection in a clinical setting for patients with caries.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adults capable of giving consent
- Presence of natural dentition or fixed dentures with approximal spaces
- Patients who agree to participate in the study
- Not physically or mentally impaired in the daily use of oral hygiene

The following inclusion criteria also apply to the respective patient groups:
- Periodontitis group: Presence of periodontitis stage 1-4
- Caries group: At least three active carious lesions requiring treatment
- Geriatric group: At least 75 years of age and multimorbid (simultaneous presence of at least three chronic diseases) or older than 80 years
Exclusion criteria:
- Presence of orthodontic appliances
- Active systematic periodontitis therapy or periodontal surgery within the last 6 months
- Known allergies to dental materials and preparations
- Patients who require assistance with oral hygiene at home
- Use of systemic antibiotics within the last 30 days
- Current nicotine use
- Current pregnancy
- Patients who do not meet the inclusion criteria
